A_target.statement: Adjoining to an [[Definition:Affine Plane|affine plane]] one point at infinity for each [[Definition:Parallel Lines|parallel class]] of lines, and one line at infinity containing exactly these points, gives a [[Definition:Projective Plane|projective plane]]: any two distinct points lie on exactly one line, and any two distinct lines meet in exactly one point.

B_source.statement: In an affine plane, any two distinct points lie on exactly one line, and through a point not on a line $\ell$ there is exactly one line parallel to $\ell$.

object_map.reformulation: Remove the exception for parallel lines by giving each direction a common point.

validity_conditions: Playfair's axiom is what makes the line through an affine point and a point at infinity unique.
Metric notions such as distance and angle do not extend to the completion.
proof_plan:
For each parallel class $\sqbrk \ell$, adjoin a point $P_{\sqbrk \ell}$ lying on every line of that class.
Adjoin a line $\ell_\infty$ consisting of all the new points.

Two distinct affine lines meet in exactly one affine point if not parallel, and in exactly their common point at infinity if parallel.
An affine line meets $\ell_\infty$ exactly in its own point at infinity.

Two affine points lie on exactly one line, by the source result.
An affine point $P$ and $P_{\sqbrk \ell}$ lie on exactly one line, the parallel to $\ell$ through $P$.
Two points at infinity lie only on $\ell_\infty$.
